description: Two things that were losing findings quietly. A CommonJS export table -- an object literal whose values NAME functions declared elsewhere -- stopped call resolution, so a tainted argument tainted the call RESULT instead of entering the callee, and everything the callee did with it went unseen; one vulnerable application hid four SQL injections behind exactly this. And a merge point kept only the first path that reached it, so a branch through a converting transform silenced a branch through none -- the value is the same value, and the finding has to rest on the branch that proves it. The negative is a merge where every branch converts.

expected.note: through the export table: the handler is in one file and the injection in another, and resolving the call is the whole of it
the source names the UNCONVERTED branch of the ternary. Both branches carry the caller's value and only one proves the finding
